body: SDCL Tennessee Propco LLC, a Delaware company with its principal place of business in New York, sued Bradley County in Chancery Court on Sept. 17, 2026, WTVC NewsChannel 9 reported after obtaining the complaint. The Chattanooga Times Free Press described the developer, SDCL, as a London-based firm with U.S. headquarters in New York City and reported that Bradley County Mayor Gary Davis shared the suit on Monday, Sept. 21. The project, Project MidSpan, is a planned data center campus on about 306 acres behind Walker Valley High School, in the Hiwassee River Industrial Park near Exit 33.

According to WTVC's account of the complaint, SDCL took an option on the land in July 2024 and bought it on April 28, 2025 for $19,904,950. At the time, all but about 2.5 acres were zoned I-1 General Industrial, which the company says permitted a large-scale data center; the suit includes a September 2022 letter from the county's planning director saying the district was appropriate for one. On April 20, 2026, commissioners voted 14-0 to allow data centers only in the I-2 Special Impact Industrial District and to bar them within 3,000 feet of an existing home, school or church. Davis said the project's nearest proposed building would be about 1,700 feet from the high school.

SDCL argues that the version commissioners approved was materially different from the one the county's regional planning commission considered and should have gone back to that commission, that the county did not give proper public notice of the final version, and that taking up the substitute without listing it on the April 20 agenda violated Tennessee's Open Meetings Act. It also claims the rules are arbitrary and discriminatory, violate equal protection and due process, and effectively exclude data centers from all of unincorporated Bradley County. It seeks a declaration that the rules are invalid, an order barring their enforcement against its property, and legal costs and attorneys' fees.

Bradley County had not yet filed a response when WTVC reported. Davis said the county will defend the regulations: "Bradley County will defend its position and the regulations adopted by your county commission."

timeline.label: SDCL enters an option agreement for about 306 acres in the Hiwassee River Industrial Park
Bradley County commissioners vote 14-0 to limit data centers to the I-2 district with a 3,000-foot setback
SDCL Tennessee Propco sues Bradley County in Chancery Court
